method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Both sheets name the seam: sheet 82's east margin prints 'AVENUE T' beside the adjoining-sheet numeral '99', and sheet 99's west margin prints 'AVENUE T' beside the adjoining numeral '82'. Sheet 82's other labelled corridors are 'AVENUE S' and 'AVENUE S 1/2', so Ave T (not S 1/2) is the shared one. The 37th and 38th St hundred-blocks settle it: on sheet 82 the blocks between Ave S and Ave S 1/2 carry the 2500 runs (2501 2503 ... 2529 / 2502 2504 ... 2524) and the block between Ave S 1/2 and Ave T carries the 2600 runs (2601 2603 2605 ... 2623 / 2602 2604 2606 ... 2624); on sheet 99 the first block east of the seam carries the 2700 runs (2701 2703 2705 2707 2709 2711, 2713 2715 2717 / 2702 2704 2706 2708 2710 2712, 2714 2716). The 2600/2700 change is exactly at Ave T. Avenue frontage numbers 3702 3704 ... 3736, 3802 3804 on sheet 82's east face and 3701 3703 3705 ... on sheet 99's west face are the two sides of the same avenue; block quarters read 'S.E. 160' (82) and 'N.E. 185' (99). Scale: '70'' is printed in the avenue corridors and '80'' in the numbered-street corridors; the measured avenue width is 212 native px (Ave S centre 1178 to Ave S 1/2 centre 2178 gives the 1000 px corridor pitch). Sheet 82's Ave T west block face is at native x 3073 (paper trimmed at 3275), centre 3179; sheet 99's east block face at native x 1893 (paper trimmed at ~1742), centre 1787. Detection candidates 1586 (sheet 82, block interior near Ave S) and 1772 (sheet 99, Seawall Blvd/beach strip) were rejected; sheet 82's third candidate 2596 lay in the 2600 block interior.
